faults.fault: At 1.7x taller the extra height went into a stretched, smeared grey/wood panel below the cabinet instead of into longer cabinet members; at 1.6x wider a dark untextured strip appears on the left side where the stretched panel runs out. Extra bulk must come from the cabinet body (side panels / bubble columns running longer), not a smeared backdrop.
Bubble-tube columns stay the same length when the prop is made taller, leaving blank side panel where the tubes should simply run longer between the arch and the base.

At 1.7x tall the prop has gained a repeat it did not have when drawn: its row profile self-correlates 0.87 at a period of 54 scanlines, against 0.42 at the drawn size. Something is being laid down more than once.
At 1.7x tall the prop has gained a dead band: 38% of its height is scanlines that do not change, against 6% when drawn. The growth is filling with flat material.

wider_means: A wider jukebox is a fatter cabinet carcass with the same single dome, title strip, mechanism and grille, just more wood either side of the central column.
taller_means: A taller jukebox is a taller cabinet body: the plain wood side panels and the vertical bubble-tube columns simply run longer between the arched top and the base, with nothing added.

faults.fault: 1.7x TALLER: the extra height did not go into the cabinet body or the bubble tubes at all -- the jukebox itself is unchanged and the entire added length is a dark smeared/streaked wood-grain panel grafted below the base, with a visible seam line where it joins the real cabinet. That is smeared background standing in for taller geometry, not a taller jukebox.
The stretched lower panel shows banding/streaking in the wood grain where it was enlarged -- a seam a player can point at. Needs mirror-mode tiling so repeats reflect instead of cutting.
1.6x WIDER: the widened sides are blank dark panels and a thin red seam/streak line runs horizontally across the left added panel where the texture repeat cuts.

Solid view and wireframe show stray flat planes floating clear of the body on the upper-left rear (dark sliver off the back-left shoulder in the shaded view; detached vertical rectangles at far left in wireframe). Geometry hanging in space off the carcass is a blocking shape fault.

In the 1.7x TALLER render the bubble tubes did not run longer between arch and base as the resize rule requires -- the tubes stay original length while background fills the gap, so the tallening produced none of the vertical extension the tubes own.

At 1.7x tall the prop has gained a repeat it did not have when drawn: its row profile self-correlates 0.87 at a period of 54 scanlines, against 0.43 at the drawn size. Something is being laid down more than once.
At 1.7x tall the prop has gained a dead band: 38% of its height is scanlines that do not change, against 6% when drawn. The growth is filling with flat material.

taller_means: A taller jukebox is a taller cabinet body: the plain wood side panels and the vertical bubble-tube columns simply run longer between the arched top and the base, with nothing added.
